back: A design in which instructions and data share the same memory and are fetched one at a time by the CPU over shared buses.
Holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched.
MAR: the address being read from or written to. MDR: the data or instruction read from (or going to) that address.
CIR: the instruction being decoded and executed. ACC: results of ALU calculations.
Address bus (one-way, CPU to memory); data bus (two-way); control bus (two-way control and timing signals).
PC → MAR → address bus → memory → data bus → MDR → CIR; the PC is incremented.
Faster clock: more cycles per second. More cores: tasks in parallel (if the work can be split). Larger cache: fewer slow fetches from RAM.
The list of all the machine code commands a particular CPU can process.
A small amount of very fast memory in or near the CPU that holds frequently used instructions and data.
